text: 🇲🇽🎨 Rejected by UNAM, 9,000 young people just got into university anyway. "Don't lose this opportunity — this access is a right." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Sept 10 A new federal platform, Educación Superior 2026, placed about 9,000 students turned away by UNAM — nearly 5,000 into the Rosario Castellanos university. In person, hybrid, or online.

🇲🇽✊ "They are heroes and heroines of Mexico." "That they feel proud of their origin, of being Mexican. That here we love them, that here we help them with whatever they need." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Sept 10 Her Independence Day message to Mexicans in the United States, as deportation raids spread fear in migrant communities.

🇲🇽🌎 "Sovereignty is not up for negotiation." "Mexico should not be an argument in the United States' election. We cooperate and help with whatever is needed — but we always seek respect, and non-confrontation." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Sept 10 After Marco Rubio said Mexico's fight against the cartels was "not nearly enough," Sheinbaum answered that Washington should not use Mexico in its November election. Homicides are down 53% since she took office.

🇲🇽🎨 Zero VAT — now for every publisher, not just bookstores. "It's much better that it's not just for one publisher, but for all publishers." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Sept 10 Books are already tax-exempt. Extending zero VAT across the whole publishing sector means the SAT forgoes about 200 million pesos a year — money that stays with the publishing houses.

🇲🇽✊ Small businesses will pay simpler taxes — and less of them. The Simplified Trust Regime ceilings rise: from 3.5 to 5 million pesos for individuals, and from 35 to 50 million for companies. An optional flat 7% VAT rate lets small firms drop complex accounting. — Finance Ministry / SAT, Mañanera, Sept 10

🇲🇽🏭 "Credit is not an expense — it's a way to grow a business." — Carlos Torres Rosas, head of Nafin & Bancomext, Mañanera, Sept 10 Mexico's development banks have issued over 112,000 loans worth roughly 315 billion pesos this term, including loans of up to 500,000 pesos for businesses scaling up.

🇲🇽🏭 Mexico is cutting the red tape that strangles small business. "With this simplification, we go from eight procedures down to a single one." — Labor Ministry, Mañanera, Sept 10 The REPSE contractor registry collapses from 8 steps to one online form; response times drop from 20 business days to 5. Aimed at firms with up to 10 workers — about 18,000 due to renew.

🇲🇽💰 <u>Mexico will spend 6.3% of its entire economy on pensions next year</u>

The 2027 budget channels 2.5 trillion pesos into pensions — 23% of all federal spending and 6.3% of GDP, up from just 3.4% in 2018, reports El Economista. That is nearly as much as education (1.4tn) and health (1.2tn) combined. The 4T's premise is simple: the elderly are not a line item to be cut, they are the reason a state exists.

🇲🇽🎆 <u>Mexico City lights the Zócalo for the women independence tried to erase</u>

Ahead of the Sept 15 independence celebrations, Clara Brugada lit the capital with 45,000 LEDs across 3,000 square meters honoring Josefa Ortiz, Leona Vicario, Gertrudis Bocanegra and "La Güera" Rodríguez — women who gave strategy, fortunes and their lives to the fight. "The homeland also had mothers," Brugada said, in a country now led by its first woman president.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Mexico has paid 1.6 trillion pesos in Fobaproa interest alone — and still owes all of it</u>

The 1994 bank bailout that Zedillo converted into public debt has cost Mexicans 1.6 trillion pesos in interest, while the principal hasn't budged. Treasury officials concede it "will hardly ever finish being paid." For the first time, the 2027 budget stops letting the banks — who still cover 75% of the IPAB quota — deduct those payments from their own taxes. A first crack in the wall neoliberalism built to make the public pay for private losses forever.
